doc.name: A — hand tools catalogue, travel context, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: forged garden secateurs
Category: hand tools
Shot programme: travel context
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the art director signing off every frame of this hand tools campaign. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the tilted dynamic in a travel context treatment.

SUBJECT. A forged garden secateurs. Treat the attached reference as the single source of truth for the product's geometry, proportion, colourway, finish and label typography. Do not redesign, restyle, re-letter or embellish it.

CAMERA. Camera rolled into a deliberate tilt with the product on a diagonal. Shoot on a 58mm vintage double-gauss at f/22, framing for rule-of-thirds weighting to frame-left with open air to the right.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with underlighting from a translucent base panel. Stage the product on or against hand-thrown ceramic, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a bleach-bypass look with crushed saturation and lifted contrast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
